page_title: Tutorial: Make web games with Phaser 3

summary.title: Tutorial: Make web games with Phaser 3
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a simple browser game in Phaser 3, covering scenes, sprites, text, arcade-physics overlap detection, keyboard input, and tweens.
takeaways: Phaser games are built from scenes with preload(), create(), and update() methods, called in that order.
Assets are loaded in preload() and sprites are placed in create(); the physics engine is enabled through this.physics.add.sprite.
Keyboard input via createCursorKeys() can move a sprite each frame inside update().
Collisions are detected with this.physics.overlap(), and a tween (this.tweens.add) can give visual feedback like a temporary scale change.
Phaser projects need to be served from a local web server (e.g. python -m http.server) rather than opened as files.
summary.summary: This step-by-step tutorial by lessmilk builds a small browser game in Phaser 3 where the player collects coins to earn points. It walks through the project setup (index.html, game.js, assets folder), defining a scene with preload, create and update methods, and creating the Phaser.Game configuration. It then adds sprites, a score text, arrow-key movement, overlap-based collision handling, and a scale tween on coin pickup. The author notes the full game is under 60 lines of code and points to a paid ebook for more.
